'''Brent Michael Jones''' (born February 12, 1963) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player, business executive, businessman, coach, and [[sports analyst]]. As a player, he was a [[tight end]] for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] during his entire 11-year career in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1987 to 1997. Jones is listed among the top players in franchise history, and helped revolutionize the concept of the pass-catching tight end.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/517220-san-francisco-49ers-top-50-greatest-49ers-of-all-time|title=San Francisco 49ers: The Top 50 Greatest 49ers of All Time|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|access-date=October 22, 2020|archive-date=October 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171028101733/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/517220-san-francisco-49ers-top-50-greatest-49ers-of-all-time|url-status=live}}</ref>

After playing [[college football]] at [[Santa Clara University]], Jones was selected 135th overall by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the fifth round of the [[1986 NFL draft]]. Cut after one season with the Steelers, he joined the 49ers during training camp in 1987. He went on to become the team's starting tight end in his third season after the retirement of [[John Frank (tight end)|John Frank]] and played with the 49ers for 11 seasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1995-01-14-sp-19956-story.html|title=Archives|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|access-date=April 16, 2020|archive-date=March 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306042650/http://articles.latimes.com/1995-01-14/sports/sp-19956_1_brent-jones|url-status=live}}</ref> He finished his 49ers career as the franchise's all-time leader in receptions (417), receiving yards (5,195) and receiving touchdowns (33) by a tight end, until [[Vernon Davis]] surpassed all three of those records. In the regular season, Jones played in 143 career games, winning 110 of them. In the playoffs, Jones played in 21 career games, starting 19 games, and winning 14 of them. Jones won nine NFC West titles with the 49ers. Jones finished his playoff career with 60 receptions for 740 receiving yards. Jones won three Super Bowls and was named All-Pro three times (1992–1994) and was selected to four Pro Bowls (1992–1995). These are all franchise records by a tight end. Jones never experienced a losing season and has one of the highest winning percentages in NFL history. [[Jerry Rice]] and Jones are considered the greatest wide receiver-tight end duo in NFL history.

'''Brent Leanrd Fullwood''' is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FullBr00.htm|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Brent Fullwood Stats}}</ref> He was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the first round (fourth overall pick) of the [[1987 NFL draft]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=1987 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1987/draft.htm |access-date=2023-09-25 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> after finishing sixth in 1986 Heisman Trophy voting.<ref name="heis">{{cite web |last1=staff |title=Winners |url=http://www.heisman.com/winners/v-testaverde86.php |website=heisman.com |access-date=13 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004225920/http://www.heisman.com/winners/v-testaverde86.php |archive-date=4 October 2013}}</ref>  

Fullwood played four [[NFL]] seasons, from 1987 to 1990. His best year as a pro came during the 1989 season, when he led the Packers in rushing with 821 yards and was selected to the [[1990 Pro Bowl]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Packers' Fullwood a Pro Bowl reserve|work=[[Sheboygan Press]]|date=January 20, 1990|page=14}}</ref> However [[Sports Illustrated]] listed Fullwood as one of the Packers biggest draft busts, noting a high rate of fumbles and a 1990 incident when he removed himself from a game against the [[Chicago Bears]] claiming illness, but was seen later that evening at a nightclub.<ref name="Huber">{{cite journal |last1=Huber |first1=Bill |title=All-Busts Team: Greatest Packers’ NFL Draft Busts of All-Time |journal=Sports Illustrated |date=12 April 2025 |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/packers/onsi/all-busts-team-greatest-packers-nfl-draft-busts-of-all-time |access-date=13 December 2025}}</ref> After this incident the Packers traded Fullwood on October 9, 1990 to the [[Cleveland Browns]] for a 7th Round draft choice, however he only dressed for one game for the Browns who waived him 2 months after signing him.<ref name="Keim">{{cite news |last1=Keim |first1=Bob |title=Fullwood waived, Rowell back again - UPI Archives |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1990/12/26/Fullwood-waived-Rowell-back-again/7635662187600/ |access-date=13 December 2025 |work=UPI |date=26 December 1990 |language=en}}</ref> During the 1991 and 1992 offseasons he was briefly signed by the Miami Dolphins and then Los Angeles Raiders but was released by both before the regular playing season began.<ref name="BN">{{cite news |last1=staff |title=Dolphins sign Brent Fullwood |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1153685489/?match=1&terms=brent%20fullwood%20miami |access-date=29 December 2025 |work=The Birmingham News |date=13 February 1991 |page=30}}</ref><ref name="Chapman">{{cite news |last1=Chapman |first1=Jeff |title=Rookies Pace 49ers Past Raiders |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/779990588/?match=1&terms=brent%20fullwood%20raiders |access-date=29 December 2025 |work=Oakland Tribune |date=9 August 1992 |page=39}}</ref>
